audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper (W) is repeatedly described as Mundo's auto-attack reset and as a channel: whys[1] "Heart Zapper's auto-reset", spikes[0].text "his Heart Zapper auto-trade does nothing", early "His Heart Zapper channels briefly before activating", wants.foe[0] "Heart Zapper's brief channel", full dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns "His sustain + reset".
audit.why: Heart Zapper is a self-cast aura: it switches on immediately, deals persistent damage to nearby enemies for its duration, stores a portion of damage taken, and bursts at the end of the duration or on recast. It has no channel and no auto reset. The auto-attack reset in Mundo's kit is Blunt Force Trauma (E) — this is exactly what _missing-interactions.json flags for this matchup. The practical consequence is the opposite of what the text says: Heart Zapper's aura damage ticks on you through a blind, so a Teemo who dumps Q on the W cast wastes it.
audit.corrected: Spend Blinding Dart on his basic attacks and the Blunt Force Trauma (E) reset wind-up, not on the Heart Zapper cast. W is an aura and will keep damaging you regardless of the blind.
sources: champ-data/_kits/drmundo.json (W Heart Zapper: 'electrocutes himself, dealing persistent damage to nearby enemies... At the end of the duration or on Recast'; flags: heal only. E Blunt Force Trauma flags: autoReset)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states Heart Zapper's or Maximum Dosage's real cooldowns, despite the whole entry being built around 'wait for his cooldown'.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15 seconds and Maximum Dosage is a flat 120 seconds at every rank — R does not get shorter as he levels it, which is the single most exploitable fact in the matchup. whys[4] and mid both say 'let the cooldown expire' without a number, so the player has no idea whether that is 40 seconds or two minutes.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper: 17s at rank 1 down to 15s at rank 5. Maximum Dosage: flat 120s at all three ranks — bait it, then own the next two minutes.

audit.whatIsWrong: early tells the player not to chase past the halfway line because of the cleaver but never states the range asymmetry that actually governs the lane.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw has 975 range on a flat 4-second cooldown; Teemo's auto and Blinding Dart are both 680. Mundo out-ranges Teemo by ~295 units and pays only health for it, so 'Teemo poke wins' is not automatic — he can trade you down from outside every tool you own. That is why the packet's level 1 is not a clean Teemo stage.
audit.corrected: Infected Bonesaw is 975 range on a 4s cooldown vs your 680 auto range, and it scales off your current health. Sidestep it rather than trying to out-poke it head-on.
sources: champ-data/_kits/drmundo.json (Q Infected Bonesaw range 975, cooldown 4, 'damage to the first enemy hit based on their current health')
champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (Q range 680, E Toxic Shot range 680)

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases (P) is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: The passive resists the first immobilising effect that hits Mundo, dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and reduce the passive's cooldown. Teemo's kit contains no immobilising effect at all — Noxious Trap slows, it does not root or stun — so in a pure 1v1 that charge is never consumed and simply sits there. It matters the moment a jungler with hard CC arrives: the first CC is eaten by the passive, so the gank must carry a second source of CC or it fails. That is a jungle-coordination fact worth saying and it is currently absent.
audit.corrected: You have no immobilising effect, so his passive charge stays up all lane. Tell your jungler: the first stun or root is eaten by Goes Where He Pleases — a one-CC gank does not stick.
sources: champ-data/_kits/drmundo.json (P: 'resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him... dropping a chemical cannister')
champ-data/_kits/teemo.json (kitFlags: no hardCC; R flags slow/zone only)

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "Q is max-ranked" at Levels 4-5.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is rank 2 at level 4 and rank 3 at level 5; it is not maxed until level 9. It is also a flat 7s cooldown at every rank, so ranking Q up is not a lane spike at all.
audit.corrected: Q is rank 2-3 at Levels 4-5; the stage advantage is shroom coverage, not a Q rank.

notes: The full layer's phases[] and the content layer's win[] disagree on Level 1 for this matchup (full says 'Dr. Mundo', content says 'Skill').
